Article 1

In this Regional Regulation what is meant by:

1. Regional Government is the Regent and Regional Apparatus as elements of the implementation of Regional Government.
2. Regent is the Regent of Madiun.
3. Child is a person who is not yet 18 years old and has never been married, including those in the womb.
4. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and worth, and receive protection from violence and discrimination
5. Violence is any act that results in or can result in suffering or distress whether physical, psychological, sexual, and economic to the victim. 6. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds, or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, unconsciousness and/or causes death.
7. Psychological violence is an act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering in a person.
8. Sexual violence is an act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial and certain purposes.
9. Victim is a woman and child who experiences suffering and/or distress either directly or indirectly as a result of violence. 10. Service is an action taken as soon as possible to the victim when seeing, hearing and knowing about, during or after the occurrence of violence against the victim.
11. Companion is a person who has the expertise to accompany victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for the empowerment and recovery of victims of violence.
12. Integrated Service Center, hereinafter abbreviated as PPT is an institution providing services to victims of violence, which is hospital-based, managed jointly in the form of medical services (including medico-legal), psycho-social and general services.
13. Safe house is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with specified operational standards. 14. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations.
15. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband, wife and their children, or father and his children, and mother and her children.
16. Household is family members and relatives (grandchildren, nephews/nieces, older siblings, younger siblings, grandfather, grandmother, cousins and so forth) and non-relatives (housemaids, drivers, and so forth) who live and eat from one kitchen and reside in one house.

CHAPTER II

PRINCIPLES AND OBJECTIVES

Article 2

The principles of organizing protection for women and children victims of violence are: 1. Respect for the rights of victims.

2. Justice and gender equality.

3. Non-discrimination.

4. The best interests of victims.

5. Respect for the rights of women and children.

Article 3

The objective of organizing protection for women and children victims of violence is to provide protection and services to women and children victims of gender-based violence and the best interests of children occurring in the household and/or public.

CHAPTER III

RIGHTS OF VICTIMS

Article 4

Every victim has the right to receive protection, information, integrated services, continuous handling up to the rehabilitation stage and confidential handling from individuals, groups or institutions, both Regency Government and non-government.

Article 5

In the event of violence, every victim has the right to receive assistance both psychologically and legally as well as to obtain guarantees of their rights related to their status as wife, mother, child, family member and as a member of society.

CHAPTER IV

OBLIGATIONS AND RESPONSIBILITIES

Article 6

(1) The Regional Government is obliged and responsible to carry out efforts to prevent the occurrence of violence, in the form of:

a. collecting data and information about women and children victims of violence as well as legislation;
b. conducting education on anti-violence values against women and children;
c. conducting socialization of legislation related to the organization of protection for women and children victims of violence; d. conducting monitoring and evaluation of the organization of protection for women and children victims of violence.
(2) To anticipate the occurrence of acts of violence, the Regional Government is obliged to provide and organize services for victims in the form of: a. establishing and facilitating the organization of integrated service institutions for victims involving community elements;
b. encouraging community awareness of the importance of protection for victims.
(3) The Regional Government in carrying out obligations as referred to in paragraphs (1) and (2) must pay attention to the rights and obligations of parents, guardians, husbands, or other persons who are legally responsible for the victim.

Article 14

This Regional Regulation shall come into effect on the date of promulgation. In order that everyone may know of it, orders the promulgation of this Regional Regulation by placing it in the Regional Gazette of Madiun Regency.

CONCERNING

ORGANIZATION OF PROTECTION

FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL ELUCIDATION

The State has the obligation to provide a sense of security to its citizens from threats and actions that can disturb or damage mental, physical, sexual or economic security, this is philosophically stated in the Preamble of the 1945 Constitution, that the first objective of the establishment of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia is to protect all the people and the entire territory of Indonesia.

Since the Government of Indonesia has signed the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR 1948) and ratified CEDAW (Law Number 7 of 1984 concerning the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women), it is obliged to comply with these provisions. Likewise in the 1945 Constitution fourth amendment chapter XA of the 1945 Constitution concerning Human Rights, it states that the enforcement and fulfillment of Human Rights is the responsibility of the state, especially the Government.

Furthermore, in the National Action Plan for the Elimination of Violence Against Women of 1999 it is stated that Women as Mothers of the nation and children as successors of the nation are creatures created by God Almighty so that their honor, dignity and self-esteem must be protected and maintained properly and proportionally, both legally, economically, politically, socially and culturally, without distinguishing ethnicity, religion, race and class.

From the series of provisions above, the Government is responsible for taking actions both legally, politically, economically and socially to prevent, suppress, reduce and eliminate all forms of violence against women and children because it constitutes a crime against human existence.

II. ELUCIDATION ARTICLE BY ARTICLE

Article 1: Sufficiently clear

Article 2

Respect for the rights of victims is intended to ensure the fulfillment of the rights of victims.

Gender justice is a process to be fair to men and women.

Gender equality is the equality of conditions for men and women to obtain opportunities and their rights as human beings, so they are able to play a role and participate in political, socio-cultural, defense and national security activities and equality in enjoying the results of development.

Non-discrimination is an attitude and treatment towards victims by not making distinctions based on age, sex, race, ethnicity, religion and between groups.

The best interests of the victim are all actions concerning victims carried out by the Government, society, legislative body and judiciary, thus the best interests of the victim must be the primary consideration.

Article 4

What is meant by receiving protection is receiving protection from individuals, groups or institutions, both government and non-government.

Receiving information about the existence of complaint centers, PPT and matters related to the fulfillment of their rights and being involved in every decision-making process related to assistance and progress in case handling.

What is meant by integrated services is services that include medical, medico-legal, psychosocial and legal.

What is meant by sustainable handling is handling that does not only stop at physical and psychological healing, but until the victim can resume their life in society including restoration of their good name.

Article 11

Assistance is carried out by persons or institutions that have the expertise to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for the empowerment and recovery of victims of violence and have cooperated with PPT.

Article 9

The organization of services for victims is carried out free of charge, quickly, safely, empathetically, non-discriminatorily, and with guarantees of confidentiality.

Article 3

What is meant by gender-based violence is actions based on gender relations that place women in a subordinate position to men.

I. GENERAL ELUCIDATION

The State has the obligation to provide a sense of security to its citizens from threats and actions that can disturb or damage mental, physical, sexual or economic security, this is philosophically stated in the Preamble of the 1945 Constitution, that the first objective of the establishment of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia is to protect all the people and the entire territory of Indonesia.

Since the Government of Indonesia has signed the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR 1948) and ratified CEDAW (Law Number 7 of 1984 concerning the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women), it is obliged to comply with these provisions. Likewise in the 1945 Constitution fourth amendment chapter XA of the 1945 Constitution concerning Human Rights, it states that the enforcement and fulfillment of Human Rights is the responsibility of the state, especially the Government.

Furthermore, in the National Action Plan for the Elimination of Violence Against Women of 1999 it is stated that Women as Mothers of the nation and children as successors of the nation are creatures created by God Almighty so that their honor, dignity and self-esteem must be protected and maintained properly and proportionally, both legally, economically, politically, socially and culturally, without distinguishing ethnicity, religion, race and class.

From the series of provisions above, the Government is responsible for taking actions both legally, politically, economically and socially to prevent, suppress, reduce and eliminate all forms of violence against women and children because it constitutes a crime against human existence.

II. ELUCIDATION ARTICLE BY ARTICLE

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation what is meant by:

1. Regional Government is the Regent and Regional Apparatus as elements of the implementation of Regional Government.
2. Regent is the Regent of Madiun.
3. Child is a person who is not yet 18 years old and has never been married, including those in the womb.
4. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and worth, and receive protection from violence and discrimination
5. Violence is any act that results in or can result in suffering or distress whether physical, psychological, sexual, and economic to the victim. 6. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds, or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, unconsciousness and/or causes death.
7. Psychological violence is an act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering in a person.
8. Sexual violence is an act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial and certain purposes.
9. Victim is a woman and child who experiences suffering and/or distress either directly or indirectly as a result of violence. 10. Service is an action taken as soon as possible to the victim when seeing, hearing and knowing about, during or after the occurrence of violence against the victim.
11. Companion is a person who has the expertise to accompany victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for the empowerment and recovery of victims of violence.
12. Integrated Service Center, hereinafter abbreviated as PPT is an institution providing services to victims of violence, which is hospital-based, managed jointly in the form of medical services (including medico-legal), psycho-social and general services.
13. Safe house is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with specified operational standards. 14. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations.
15. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband, wife and their children, or father and his children, and mother and her children.
16. Household is family members and relatives (grandchildren, nephews/nieces, older siblings, younger siblings, grandfather, grandmother, cousins and so forth) and non-relatives (housemaids, drivers, and so forth) who live and eat from one kitchen and reside in one house.

NUMBER 5 OF 2008

CONCERNING

ORGANIZATION OF PROTECTION

FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL ELUCIDATION

The State has the obligation to provide a sense of security to its citizens from threats and actions that can disturb or damage mental, physical, sexual or economic security, this is philosophically stated in the Preamble of the 1945 Constitution, that the first objective of the establishment of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia is to protect all the people and the entire territory of Indonesia.

Since the Government of Indonesia has signed the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR 1948) and ratified CEDAW (Law Number 7 of 1984 concerning the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women), it is obliged to comply with these provisions. Likewise in the 1945 Constitution fourth amendment chapter XA of the 1945 Constitution concerning Human Rights, it states that the enforcement and fulfillment of Human Rights is the responsibility of the state, especially the Government.

Furthermore, in the National Action Plan for the Elimination of Violence Against Women of 1999 it is stated that Women as Mothers of the nation and children as successors of the nation are creatures created by God Almighty so that their honor, dignity and self-esteem must be protected and maintained properly and proportionally, both legally, economically, politically, socially and culturally, without distinguishing ethnicity, religion, race and class.

From the series of provisions above, the Government is responsible for taking actions both legally, politically, economically and socially to prevent, suppress, reduce and eliminate all forms of violence against women and children because it constitutes a crime against human existence.

II. ELUCIDATION ARTICLE BY ARTICLE

Article 1: Sufficiently clear

Article 2

Respect for the rights of victims is intended to ensure the fulfillment of the rights of victims.

Gender justice is a process to be fair to men and women.

Gender equality is the equality of conditions for men and women to obtain opportunities and their rights as human beings, so they are able to play a role and participate in political, socio-cultural, defense and national security activities and equality in enjoying the results of development.

Non-discrimination is an attitude and treatment towards victims by not making distinctions based on age, sex, race, ethnicity, religion and between groups.

The best interests of the victim are all actions concerning victims carried out by the Government, society, legislative body and judiciary, thus the best interests of the victim must be the primary consideration.

Article 3

What is meant by gender-based violence is actions based on gender relations that place women in a subordinate position to men.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation what is meant by:

1. Regional Government is the Regent and Regional Apparatus as elements of the implementation of Regional Government.
2. Regent is the Regent of Madiun.
3. Child is a person who is not yet 18 years old and has never been married, including those in the womb.
4. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and worth, and receive protection from violence and discrimination
5. Violence is any act that results in or can result in suffering or distress whether physical, psychological, sexual, and economic to the victim. 6. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds, or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, unconsciousness and/or causes death.
7. Psychological violence is an act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering in a person.
8. Sexual violence is an act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial and certain purposes.
9. Victim is a woman and child who experiences suffering and/or distress either directly or indirectly as a result of violence. 10. Service is an action taken as soon as possible to the victim when seeing, hearing and knowing about, during or after the occurrence of violence against the victim.
11. Companion is a person who has the expertise to accompany victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for the empowerment and recovery of victims of violence.
12. Integrated Service Center, hereinafter abbreviated as PPT is an institution providing services to victims of violence, which is hospital-based, managed jointly in the form of medical services (including medico-legal), psycho-social and general services.
13. Safe house is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with specified operational standards. 14. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations.
15. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband, wife and their children, or father and his children, and mother and her children.
16. Household is family members and relatives (grandchildren, nephews/nieces, older siblings, younger siblings, grandfather, grandmother, cousins and so forth) and non-relatives (housemaids, drivers, and so forth) who live and eat from one kitchen and reside in one house.

Article 2

The principles of organizing protection for women and children victims of violence are: 1. Respect for the rights of victims.

2. Justice and gender equality.

3. Non-discrimination.

4. The best interests of victims.

5. Respect for the rights of women and children.

Article 3

The objective of organizing protection for women and children victims of violence is to provide protection and services to women and children victims of gender-based violence and the best interests of children occurring in the household and/or public.

CHAPTER III

RIGHTS OF VICTIMS

Article 4

Every victim has the right to receive protection, information, integrated services, continuous handling up to the rehabilitation stage and confidential handling from individuals, groups or institutions, both Regency Government and non-government.

Article 5

In the event of violence, every victim has the right to receive assistance both psychologically and legally as well as to obtain guarantees of their rights related to their status as wife, mother, child, family member and as a member of society.

CHAPTER IV

OBLIGATIONS AND RESPONSIBILITIES

Article 6

(1) The Regional Government is obliged and responsible to carry out efforts to prevent the occurrence of violence, in the form of:

a. collecting data and information about women and children victims of violence as well as legislation;
b. conducting education on anti-violence values against women and children;
c. conducting socialization of legislation related to the organization of protection for women and children victims of violence; d. conducting monitoring and evaluation of the organization of protection for women and children victims of violence.
(2) To anticipate the occurrence of acts of violence, the Regional Government is obliged to provide and organize services for victims in the form of: a. establishing and facilitating the organization of integrated service institutions for victims involving community elements;
b. encouraging community awareness of the importance of protection for victims.
(3) The Regional Government in carrying out obligations as referred to in paragraphs (1) and (2) must pay attention to the rights and obligations of parents, guardians, husbands, or other persons who are legally responsible for the victim.

Article 10

PPT managers are obliged to organize services in accordance with the service principles as referred to in Article 9.

Article 14

This Regional Regulation shall come into effect on the date of promulgation. In order that everyone may know of it, orders the promulgation of this Regional Regulation by placing it in the Regional Gazette of Madiun Regency.

The principles of organizing protection for women and children victims of violence are: 1. Respect for the rights of victims.

The objective of organizing protection for women and children victims of violence is to provide protection and services to women and children victims of gender-based violence and the best interests of children occurring in the household and/or public.

CHAPTER III

RIGHTS OF VICTIMS

Article 4

Every victim has the right to receive protection, information, integrated services, continuous handling up to the rehabilitation stage and confidential handling from individuals, groups or institutions, both Regency Government and non-government.

Article 5

In the event of violence, every victim has the right to receive assistance both psychologically and legally as well as to obtain guarantees of their rights related to their status as wife, mother, child, family member and as a member of society.

CHAPTER IV

OBLIGATIONS AND RESPONSIBILITIES

Article 6

(1) The Regional Government is obliged and responsible to carry out efforts to prevent the occurrence of violence, in the form of:

a. collecting data and information about women and children victims of violence as well as legislation;
b. conducting education on anti-violence values against women and children;
c. conducting socialization of legislation related to the organization of protection for women and children victims of violence; d. conducting monitoring and evaluation of the organization of protection for women and children victims of violence.
(2) To anticipate the occurrence of acts of violence, the Regional Government is obliged to provide and organize services for victims in the form of: a. establishing and facilitating the organization of integrated service institutions for victims involving community elements;
b. encouraging community awareness of the importance of protection for victims.
(3) The Regional Government in carrying out obligations as referred to in paragraphs (1) and (2) must pay attention to the rights and obligations of parents, guardians, husbands, or other persons who are legally responsible for the victim.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation what is meant by:

1. Regional Government is the Regent and Regional Apparatus as elements of the implementation of Regional Government.
2. Regent is the Regent of Madiun.
3. Child is a person who is not yet 18 years old and has never been married, including those in the womb.
4. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and worth, and receive protection from violence and discrimination
5. Violence is any act that results in or can result in suffering or distress whether physical, psychological, sexual, and economic to the victim. 6. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds, or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, unconsciousness and/or causes death.
7. Psychological violence is an act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering in a person.
8. Sexual violence is an act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial and certain purposes.
9. Victim is a woman and child who experiences suffering and/or distress either directly or indirectly as a result of violence. 10. Service is an action taken as soon as possible to the victim when seeing, hearing and knowing about, during or after the occurrence of violence against the victim.
11. Companion is a person who has the expertise to accompany victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for the empowerment and recovery of victims of violence.
12. Integrated Service Center, hereinafter abbreviated as PPT is an institution providing services to victims of violence, which is hospital-based, managed jointly in the form of medical services (including medico-legal), psycho-social and general services.
13. Safe house is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with specified operational standards. 14. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations.
15. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband, wife and their children, or father and his children, and mother and her children.
16. Household is family members and relatives (grandchildren, nephews/nieces, older siblings, younger siblings, grandfather, grandmother, cousins and so forth) and non-relatives (housemaids, drivers, and so forth) who live and eat from one kitchen and reside in one house.

Article 14

This Regional Regulation shall come into effect on the date of promulgation. In order that everyone may know of it, orders the promulgation of this Regional Regulation by placing it in the Regional Gazette of Madiun Regency.

Since the Government of Indonesia has signed the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR 1948) and ratified CEDAW (Law Number 7 of 1984 concerning the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women), it is obliged to comply with these provisions. From the series of provisions above, the Government is responsible for taking actions both legally, politically, economically and socially to prevent, suppress, reduce and eliminate all forms of violence against women and children because it constitutes a crime against human existence.

RIGHTS OF VICTIMS

Every victim has the right to receive protection, information, integrated services, continuous handling up to the rehabilitation stage and confidential handling from individuals, groups or institutions, both Regency Government and non-government.

In the event of violence, every victim has the right to receive assistance both psychologically and legally as well as to obtain guarantees of their rights related to their status as wife, mother, child, family member and as a member of society.

CHAPTER IV

OBLIGATIONS AND RESPONSIBILITIES

Article 6

(1) The Regional Government is obliged and responsible to carry out efforts to prevent the occurrence of violence, in the form of:

a. collecting data and information about women and children victims of violence as well as legislation;
b. conducting education on anti-violence values against women and children;
c. conducting socialization of legislation related to the organization of protection for women and children victims of violence; d. conducting monitoring and evaluation of the organization of protection for women and children victims of violence.
(2) To anticipate the occurrence of acts of violence, the Regional Government is obliged to provide and organize services for victims in the form of: a. establishing and facilitating the organization of integrated service institutions for victims involving community elements;
b. encouraging community awareness of the importance of protection for victims.

Article 4

What is meant by receiving protection is receiving protection from individuals, groups or institutions, both government and non-government.

Receiving information about the existence of complaint centers, PPT and matters related to the fulfillment of their rights and being involved in every decision-making process related to assistance and progress in case handling.

What is meant by integrated services is services that include medical, medico-legal, psychosocial and legal.

What is meant by sustainable handling is handling that does not only stop at physical and psychological healing, but until the victim can resume their life in society including restoration of their good name.

Service Principles

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation what is meant by:

1. Regional Government is the Regent and Regional Apparatus as elements of the implementation of Regional Government.

5. Violence is any act that results in or can result in suffering or distress whether physical, psychological, sexual, and economic to the victim. 6. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds, or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, unconsciousness and/or causes death.
7. Psychological violence is an act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering in a person.
8. Sexual violence is an act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial and certain purposes.
9. Victim is a woman and child who experiences suffering and/or distress either directly or indirectly as a result of violence. 10. Service is an action taken as soon as possible to the victim when seeing, hearing and knowing about, during or after the occurrence of violence against the victim.

15. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband, wife and their children, or father and his children, and mother and her children.

Article 4

CHAPTER IV

OBLIGATIONS AND RESPONSIBILITIES

Article 6

(1) The Regional Government is obliged and responsible to carry out efforts to prevent the occurrence of violence, in the form of:

a. collecting data and information about women and children victims of violence as well as legislation;
b. conducting education on anti-violence values against women and children;
c. conducting socialization of legislation related to the organization of protection for women and children victims of violence; d. conducting monitoring and evaluation of the organization of protection for women and children victims of violence.
(2) To anticipate the occurrence of acts of violence, the Regional Government is obliged to provide and organize services for victims in the form of: a. establishing and facilitating the organization of integrated service institutions for victims involving community elements;
b. encouraging community awareness of the importance of protection for victims.
(3) The Regional Government in carrying out obligations as referred to in paragraphs (1) and (2) must pay attention to the rights and obligations of parents, guardians, husbands, or other persons who are legally responsible for the victim.

Article 4

Receiving information about the existence of complaint centers, PPT and matters related to the fulfillment of their rights and being involved in every decision-making process related to assistance and progress in case handling.

What is meant by integrated services is services that include medical, medico-legal, psychosocial and legal.

What is meant by sustainable handling is handling that does not only stop at physical and psychological healing, but until the victim can resume their life in society including restoration of their good name.

Article 1

5. Violence is any act that results in or can result in suffering or distress whether physical, psychological, sexual, and economic to the victim. 6. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds, or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, unconsciousness and/or causes death.
7. Psychological violence is an act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering in a person.
8. Sexual violence is an act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial and certain purposes.
9. Victim is a woman and child who experiences suffering and/or distress either directly or indirectly as a result of violence. 10. Service is an action taken as soon as possible to the victim when seeing, hearing and knowing about, during or after the occurrence of violence against the victim.
11. Companion is a person who has the expertise to accompany victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for the empowerment and recovery of victims of violence.

Since the Government of Indonesia has signed the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR 1948) and ratified CEDAW (Law Number 7 of 1984 concerning the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women), it is obliged to comply with these provisions. NUMBER 5 OF 2008

CONCERNING

ORGANIZATION OF PROTECTION

FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL ELUCIDATION

The State has the obligation to provide a sense of security to its citizens from threats and actions that can disturb or damage mental, physical, sexual or economic security, this is philosophically stated in the Preamble of the 1945 Constitution, that the first objective of the establishment of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia is to protect all the people and the entire territory of Indonesia.

Since the Government of Indonesia has signed the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR 1948) and ratified CEDAW (Law Number 7 of 1984 concerning the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women), it is obliged to comply with these provisions. Likewise in the 1945 Constitution fourth amendment chapter XA of the 1945 Constitution concerning Human Rights, it states that the enforcement and fulfillment of Human Rights is the responsibility of the state, especially the Government.

Furthermore, in the National Action Plan for the Elimination of Violence Against Women of 1999 it is stated that Women as Mothers of the nation and children as successors of the nation are creatures created by God Almighty so that their honor, dignity and self-esteem must be protected and maintained properly and proportionally, both legally, economically, politically, socially and culturally, without distinguishing ethnicity, religion, race and class.

From the series of provisions above, the Government is responsible for taking actions both legally, politically, economically and socially to prevent, suppress, reduce and eliminate all forms of violence against women and children because it constitutes a crime against human existence.

II. ELUCIDATION ARTICLE BY ARTICLE

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation what is meant by:

1. Regional Government is the Regent and Regional Apparatus as elements of the implementation of Regional Government.
2. Regent is the Regent of Madiun.
3. Child is a person who is not yet 18 years old and has never been married, including those in the womb.
4. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and worth, and receive protection from violence and discrimination
5. Violence is any act that results in or can result in suffering or distress whether physical, psychological, sexual, and economic to the victim. 6. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds, or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, unconsciousness and/or causes death.
7. Psychological violence is an act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering in a person.
8. Sexual violence is an act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial and certain purposes.
9. Victim is a woman and child who experiences suffering and/or distress either directly or indirectly as a result of violence. 10. Service is an action taken as soon as possible to the victim when seeing, hearing and knowing about, during or after the occurrence of violence against the victim.
11. Companion is a person who has the expertise to accompany victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for the empowerment and recovery of victims of violence.
12. Integrated Service Center, hereinafter abbreviated as PPT is an institution providing services to victims of violence, which is hospital-based, managed jointly in the form of medical services (including medico-legal), psycho-social and general services.
13. Safe house is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with specified operational standards. 14. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations.
15. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband, wife and their children, or father and his children, and mother and her children.
16. Household is family members and relatives (grandchildren, nephews/nieces, older siblings, younger siblings, grandfather, grandmother, cousins and so forth) and non-relatives (housemaids, drivers, and so forth) who live and eat from one kitchen and reside in one house.

Article 1: Sufficiently clear

Article 2

Respect for the rights of victims is intended to ensure the fulfillment of the rights of victims.

Gender justice is a process to be fair to men and women.

Gender equality is the equality of conditions for men and women to obtain opportunities and their rights as human beings, so they are able to play a role and participate in political, socio-cultural, defense and national security activities and equality in enjoying the results of development.

Non-discrimination is an attitude and treatment towards victims by not making distinctions based on age, sex, race, ethnicity, religion and between groups.

The best interests of the victim are all actions concerning victims carried out by the Government, society, legislative body and judiciary, thus the best interests of the victim must be the primary consideration.

CHAPTER V

ORGANIZATION OF PROTECTION

Part One

Institutional

Article 4

What is meant by receiving protection is receiving protection from individuals, groups or institutions, both government and non-government.

Receiving information about the existence of complaint centers, PPT and matters related to the fulfillment of their rights and being involved in every decision-making process related to assistance and progress in case handling.

What is meant by integrated services is services that include medical, medico-legal, psychosocial and legal.

What is meant by sustainable handling is handling that does not only stop at physical and psychological healing, but until the victim can resume their life in society including restoration of their good name.

Article 3

What is meant by gender-based violence is actions based on gender relations that place women in a subordinate position to men.

PRINCIPLES AND OBJECTIVES

Article 2

The principles of organizing protection for women and children victims of violence are: 1. Respect for the rights of victims.

3. Non-discrimination.

4. The best interests of victims.

5. Respect for the rights of women and children.

Article 3

The objective of organizing protection for women and children victims of violence is to provide protection and services to women and children victims of gender-based violence and the best interests of children occurring in the household and/or public.

CHAPTER III

RIGHTS OF VICTIMS

Article 4

Every victim has the right to receive protection, information, integrated services, continuous handling up to the rehabilitation stage and confidential handling from individuals, groups or institutions, both Regency Government and non-government.

Article 5

In the event of violence, every victim has the right to receive assistance both psychologically and legally as well as to obtain guarantees of their rights related to their status as wife, mother, child, family member and as a member of society.

CHAPTER IV

OBLIGATIONS AND RESPONSIBILITIES

Article 6

(1) The Regional Government is obliged and responsible to carry out efforts to prevent the occurrence of violence, in the form of:

a. collecting data and information about women and children victims of violence as well as legislation;
b. conducting education on anti-violence values against women and children;
c. conducting socialization of legislation related to the organization of protection for women and children victims of violence; d. conducting monitoring and evaluation of the organization of protection for women and children victims of violence.
(2) To anticipate the occurrence of acts of violence, the Regional Government is obliged to provide and organize services for victims in the form of: a. establishing and facilitating the organization of integrated service institutions for victims involving community elements;
b. encouraging community awareness of the importance of protection for victims.
(3) The Regional Government in carrying out obligations as referred to in paragraphs (1) and (2) must pay attention to the rights and obligations of parents, guardians, husbands, or other persons who are legally responsible for the victim.

I. GENERAL ELUCIDATION

The State has the obligation to provide a sense of security to its citizens from threats and actions that can disturb or damage mental, physical, sexual or economic security, this is philosophically stated in the Preamble of the 1945 Constitution, that the first objective of the establishment of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia is to protect all the people and the entire territory of Indonesia.

Since the Government of Indonesia has signed the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR 1948) and ratified CEDAW (Law Number 7 of 1984 concerning the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women), it is obliged to comply with these provisions. Likewise in the 1945 Constitution fourth amendment chapter XA of the 1945 Constitution concerning Human Rights, it states that the enforcement and fulfillment of Human Rights is the responsibility of the state, especially the Government.

Furthermore, in the National Action Plan for the Elimination of Violence Against Women of 1999 it is stated that Women as Mothers of the nation and children as successors of the nation are creatures created by God Almighty so that their honor, dignity and self-esteem must be protected and maintained properly and proportionally, both legally, economically, politically, socially and culturally, without distinguishing ethnicity, religion, race and class.

From the series of provisions above, the Government is responsible for taking actions both legally, politically, economically and socially to prevent, suppress, reduce and eliminate all forms of violence against women and children because it constitutes a crime against human existence.

II. ELUCIDATION ARTICLE BY ARTICLE

Article 9

The organization of services for victims is carried out free of charge, quickly, safely, empathetically, non-discriminatorily, and with guarantees of confidentiality.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation what is meant by:

1. Regional Government is the Regent and Regional Apparatus as elements of the implementation of Regional Government.
2. Regent is the Regent of Madiun.
3. Child is a person who is not yet 18 years old and has never been married, including those in the womb.
4. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and worth, and receive protection from violence and discrimination
5. Violence is any act that results in or can result in suffering or distress whether physical, psychological, sexual, and economic to the victim. 6. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds, or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, unconsciousness and/or causes death.
7. Psychological violence is an act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering in a person.
8. Sexual violence is an act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial and certain purposes.
9. Victim is a woman and child who experiences suffering and/or distress either directly or indirectly as a result of violence. 10. Service is an action taken as soon as possible to the victim when seeing, hearing and knowing about, during or after the occurrence of violence against the victim.
11. Companion is a person who has the expertise to accompany victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for the empowerment and recovery of victims of violence.
12. Integrated Service Center, hereinafter abbreviated as PPT is an institution providing services to victims of violence, which is hospital-based, managed jointly in the form of medical services (including medico-legal), psycho-social and general services.
13. Safe house is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with specified operational standards. 14. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations.
15. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband, wife and their children, or father and his children, and mother and her children.
16. Household is family members and relatives (grandchildren, nephews/nieces, older siblings, younger siblings, grandfather, grandmother, cousins and so forth) and non-relatives (housemaids, drivers, and so forth) who live and eat from one kitchen and reside in one house.
